title: Lull-to-Surge Deploy Roadmap & Pocket Notes
content:
Purpose: quick working playbook for 'lull->surge' deployments where traffic is expected to be low at start of window and may ramp fast later. Focus is minimal operator overhead at start, fast detection and automated containment during surge.

Quick notes to self: this is intentionally short — use as the on-call pocket guide during the 48h launch window. Not a full runbook.

High-level rollout pattern (recommended):
- Phase 0: Preflight (T-72 to T-8) — validation and quiet-window prep.
  - Validate canary infra: autoscaler config, instance types, model variants pinned.
  - Run smoke-suite against staging with live KV cache warmed.
  - Lock dep changes: no infra changes within T-24 unless emergency.
  - Confirm observability hooks in PR (OBS-1437).

- Phase 1: Micro-canary (T+0 to T+2 hours) — 0.5% traffic to new variant, latency SLOs prioritized.
  - Canary checks (automated + manual quick check): 200 synthetic requests, 95th lat < target, error rate < 0.2%.
  - Telemetry queries (prometheus style) to snapshot:
    - request_latency_seconds:95m{route="/generate"} < TARGET
    - jwt_rate_errors_total / request_total < 0.002
    - model_token_cost_avg / request < baseline*1.1
  - Slack pings to #release-ops with snapshot link and the simple "green/amber/red" tag.

- Phase 2: Slow ramp (T+2 to T+6 hours) — step to 2% then 10% (or predefined steps).
  - At every step, run sample-text-eval set (small set of prod prompts) and check quality regression metric (BLEU-ish / embedding-sim). If quality drop > 2.5%, pause ramp and trigger rollback.
  - Auto-throttle rules: if 95th latency > +30% baseline OR error rate > 0.5% for 3m, cut target down by 50% immediately.

- Phase 3: Surge watch (T+6 to T+48) — allow traffic to surge, keep watch on capacity fences.
  - Autoscaler floor set to ensure cold-start headroom; pre-bake instances when predicted qps > threshold.
  - If queue depth > 20s average or pending requests > X (see linked_artifacts), move to emergency containment.

Containment & rollback matrix (quick):
- Telemetry-only containment: reduce concurrency limits and enable stricter batching.
- Soft rollback: reroute to fallback model variant (lower-cost quantized variant) until traffic stabilizes.
- Hard rollback: revert to previous revision and trigger postmortem-runbook.
- Communication ladder: pager -> #release-ops -> exec on-call (if major customer-facing impact).

Checklist (preflight snapshot):
- [ ] Release branch built & artifacts uploaded to bucket (sha noted).
- [ ] Canary route configured and smoke tests green.
- [ ] Runbook pinned to #release-ops as pinned message.
- [ ] Stakeholders notified: Eng, SRE, CS on-call, Account Execs for high-value customers.
- [ ] Blackout windows confirmed with support rotations (no big product updates right after window).

Calendar (compact week-of view) — example schedule for a weekday lull->surge window: 
- Day -3: Final validation of telemetry alerts and synthetic tests.
- Day -1: Lockdown and dry-run of canary cut in staging.
- Day 0 08:00: Preflight checklist 1st pass.
- Day 0 10:00: Deploy canary (0.5%) + 30m automated smoke.
- Day 0 12:00: Ramp to 2% if green + sample eval.
- Day 0 16:00: Ramp to 10% if green.
- Day 1 00:00 to Day 2 00:00: Surge watch window (on-call presence: 09:00-21:00 primary, 21:00-03:00 reduced overlap).

Telemetry & signals (practical snippets):
- Baseline capture: take 30m preflight snapshot for request lat, p95, peak CPU/GPU util, and cost-per-token. Store as baseline-tagged graphs.
- Quick PromQLs to paste in Slack if need be: 
  - rate(http_requests_total{job="api",status!~"2.."}[5m])
  - histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
  - avg_over_time(gpu_utilization_percent[10m]) > 0.85 -> consider scale-out

Release notes (draft to copy into release digest):
- Title: "lull->surge: staged rollout of model-serving improvements (release-REL-2123)"
- Summary: "This release updates the serving runtime with improved KV cache hotpath and adds an autoscaler backoff for noisy sequences. Expected user impact: lower tail latency during moderate loads; transparent to most customers."
- Notable changes: "KV cache refactor, autoscaler smoothing, model variant pinning support."
- Rollout plan: "Micro-canary -> slow ramp -> surge watch over 48h. See runbook for signal thresholds."
- Action for customers: "No action required. If you experience degraded latency or incorrect outputs, open REL-2123 in support."

Post-release quick retro prompts (to fill in within 24h):
- What surprised us?
- Did automated throttles trigger? If yes, why?
- Which telemetry gaps hampered decision making?
- Anything to add to the smoke-suite?

Open questions / TODOs:
- Add one-click rollback dashboard (tied to the canary route) — stubbed in OBS-1437.
- Decide if sample-eval set should be extended for LLM hallucination checks.
- Document exact pending-request threshold numeric (ticketed).

Links / references:
- OBS ticket with alert rules: JIRA:OBS-1437
- Release work ticket: JIRA:REL-2123
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6789

Aisha notes: keep this minimal and actionable. If adding long explanations, move to Confluence and link here. Use this doc as the short checklist for on-call and ops leading the lull->surge window.

--- end of pocket notes ---
